tasks.name: The Weather App
tasks.text: Ollie opens the weather app on Mum's phone. A grey cloud with three drops appears on the screen. Rain all day, he reads. He is disappointed because football practice is outside. But the app also shows a small sun for tomorrow. Mum says: Weather changes quickly here. Take your umbrella and a warm jacket. At breakfast the sky is still bright. By the time the children reach school, however, the first drops fall on the pavement. Ollie opens his umbrella with a proud smile. The weather app was right after all.

tasks.name: What to Wear
tasks.text: Sophie stands in front of the wardrobe. The forecast says wind, rain and maybe a little sun. Perfect weather for layers, says Mum. Sophie chooses a T-shirt, a warm sweater and a light raincoat. She adds a bright scarf and her old boots. Ollie cannot find his other boot, and Buddy is sleeping on it. Bad dog! laughs Ollie. Jack takes a cap because he is going running. Mum checks everyone at the door: umbrella, boots, scarf. You look like a weather team! she says. Outside the wind is strong, but the family is ready for it.

tasks.name: The Windy Park
tasks.text: After school the wind is so strong that the trees bend. Ollie and George take their kites to the park. George's kite is red, Ollie's is blue with a long tail. They run across the grass and let the wind lift the kites higher and higher. A gust pulls George forward, and he almost falls. Careful! shouts Ollie. Leaves fly around them like small birds. Buddy barks at the kites and tries to catch the tails. An old man on a bench laughs: I have not seen such a windy day for years! The boys fly until their arms are tired.

tasks.name: A Rainbow
tasks.text: The rain stops as suddenly as it began. The sun comes out from behind a cloud, and a rainbow appears over the roofs. Look! shouts Sophie. Everyone runs to the balcony. The rainbow is bright and perfect, with all its colours. Mrs. Carter calls from the floor above: Quickly, take a photo before it disappears! Dad takes three pictures, but the rainbow fades little by little. Emily says: Maybe it is still there, just invisible. Mum smiles: That is a lovely idea. The family stays on the balcony and watches the wet city shine.

tasks.name: The First Frost
tasks.text: One morning the grass is white with frost. Ollie runs outside in his slippers and immediately runs back. It is freezing! The puddles near the entrance are covered with thin ice. Sophie touches it with her boot, and the ice cracks like glass. Grandpa calls from the village: Cover the young apple trees tonight. Dad finds old blankets for the garden. Mum makes hot tea with honey and lemon. The cat refuses to leave the warm radiator. Winter is not here yet, says Mum, but it is already knocking on the door.

tasks.name: No Football Today
tasks.text: Ollie wakes up early because today is the big football match. But when he looks out of the window, the yard is grey and the rain is drumming on the roof. The match is cancelled. Ollie sits on the floor and sighs. George calls him: It is only rain. We can play another day. But Ollie has waited all week. Mum makes pancakes and says: A rainy day can be a good day too. You just need a new plan. Ollie looks at the board games on the shelf. Maybe she is right. He calls George and invites him over.

tasks.name: Board Games
tasks.text: Soon the living room is full of players. George brings a box of cards, Sophie chooses a board game about travellers, and Jack joins them. The game is simple: answer questions and move around the world. George knows many capitals, but Sophie is faster with flags. Ollie lands on a difficult question: What is the longest river in the world? He thinks hard. The Nile? Everyone claps. Bella jumps onto the board and lies on Africa. The game stops while they move the cat. Mum brings sandwiches and tea.

tasks.name: Baking with Dad
tasks.text: In the afternoon Dad and Ollie decide to bake cookies. They find Grandma's recipe in an old notebook. Flour, butter, sugar, eggs and a little cinnamon. Ollie measures the flour and covers half the table. Dad laughs: Baking is also a science. You must be precise. They mix the dough, and Ollie cuts out stars, hearts and one strange dinosaur. While the cookies are in the oven, the kitchen smells wonderful. Sophie comes in and takes two before they cool. Dad pretends not to see.

tasks.name: Puddles and Boots
tasks.text: The rain becomes lighter, and Ollie cannot stay inside any longer. He puts on his boots and calls George. The yard is full of puddles, and each one is a small sea. The boys jump from puddle to puddle, making big splashes. George slips and lands on the wet grass, but he laughs. Buddy runs after them and drinks from a puddle. A neighbour opens her window and shouts: You will catch a cold! But the boys are wearing raincoats and boots. They build a small dam with sticks and watch the water change direction.

tasks.name: A Warm Evening
tasks.text: In the evening the rain returns, but now nobody minds. Mum makes a big pot of soup, and Dad lights a candle on the table. The family sits together in warm socks. Ollie tells about the puddles, and Sophie shows the cookies shaped like dinosaurs. Jack puts on soft music. Bella sleeps on the radiator, and Buddy lies under the table, hoping for crumbs. After dinner they watch an old film under a blanket. The wind blows outside, and the rain taps on the window. It feels good to be home.

tasks.name: White Morning
tasks.text: Ollie wakes up and sees a strange light in the room. Everything is white and quiet. Snow! He runs to the window and presses his nose to the glass. The yard, the cars and the roofs have disappeared under a thick white blanket. Buddy barks at the falling flakes and tries to catch them with his mouth. Sophie comes in with a blanket around her shoulders and smiles. School may start later today, says Mum. The children cheer. At breakfast they watch the snow fall and fall. The city looks like a giant birthday cake.
words: to press your nose to the glass

tasks.name: Building a Snowman
tasks.text: After breakfast the whole family goes out. The snow is perfect for a snowman. Ollie rolls a small ball until it becomes big. George pushes it across the yard. They build the second ball and lift it on top. Sophie finds a carrot for the nose and two stones for the eyes. Dad gives his old scarf, and Mum brings a hat. The snowman looks serious and a little surprised. Emily gives him a name: Mr. Frost. Buddy is not sure about the new neighbour and barks at him. Everyone laughs.

tasks.name: Sledding
tasks.text: Behind the school there is a small hill. Today it is white and crowded with children. Ollie and George bring an old wooden sled from the garage. The first ride is fast and bumpy. Snow flies into their faces, and they shout with joy. Then Emily wants to try. She is a little afraid, so Ollie sits behind her and holds the rope. Ready? Go! The sled flies down the hill, and Emily laughs all the way. At the bottom they fall into a soft snowdrift. Dad takes a photo for the family album.

tasks.name: Snowflakes
tasks.text: Sophie wants to draw a snowflake, but every one she makes looks different. That is the point, says Mr. White at art school. Real snowflakes are never the same. He shows the class photos taken with a microscope. The children see stars, needles and tiny wheels of ice. Sophie takes black paper and a white pencil. She draws slowly, line by line. Emily sits next to her and copies the pattern. Their snowflakes are not perfect, but they are beautiful. At home Sophie hangs them on the window.

tasks.name: Warm Tea by the Window
tasks.text: In the evening the snow is still falling. The family gathers in the living room with tea and biscuits. Grandma calls from the village and says their road is also white. Grandpa has already cleared a path to the gate. Ollie tells them about the sled and the snowman. Sophie promises to send a drawing. After the call, Dad puts another log in the stove. Bella sits on the windowsill and watches the flakes. Buddy sleeps near the warm radiator. Mum opens a book of winter stories.
words: to gather in the living room
to put a log in the stove

tasks.name: The Longest Day
tasks.text: June brings the longest day of the year. The sun stays in the sky until late in the evening. The family walks to the park after dinner. Children play football, and older people sit on benches and talk. The ice-cream van plays the same little song. Ollie and Sophie lie on the grass and watch the clouds turn pink. Mum says: In winter this park is dark at five o'clock. Jack answers: That is why summer feels like a gift. They stay until the first stars appear.

tasks.name: A Letter from Sydney
tasks.text: A thick envelope arrives from Australia. It is from Mrs. Carter's sister, who lives in Sydney. Inside there are photos of the sea, a koala and a very big bridge. She invites the Carter family to visit in December. Emily reads the letter aloud. George says: December is summer there! Ollie cannot imagine winter without snow. Mrs. Carter smiles: Christmas on the beach is strange, but nice. The children look at the photos and ask many questions. Maybe one day the whole family will travel to Australia.

tasks.name: The Garden Project
tasks.text: Grandma sends a box of seeds from the village. There are tomatoes, cucumbers, sunflowers and tiny apple seeds. The children decide to make a garden on the balcony. Dad brings pots and soil, and Mum finds old gloves. Ollie puts the seeds in the earth and waters them every morning. Sophie draws a sign for each pot. After a week the first green shoots appear. Ollie is so happy that he calls Grandma immediately. She says: Now be patient. A garden teaches you to wait. Every day the plants grow a little.

tasks.name: Camping by the Lake
tasks.text: At the end of July the family goes camping by a lake. Dad puts up the tent while Mum checks the food. Ollie and Sophie collect dry branches for the fire. In the evening they cook soup over the flames and watch the sun set behind the trees. The lake becomes dark and quiet. Jack shows Ollie the stars and tells him the names of three constellations. Then they hear a strange sound in the bushes. Everyone freezes. A small hedgehog comes out and looks at them. Ollie laughs with relief.

tasks.name: Last Day of Summer
tasks.text: The last day of August is warm and golden. School starts tomorrow. The children pack their bags and find clean uniforms. Ollie is sad that summer is over, but also excited about seeing his friends. The family spends the evening on the balcony. Tomatoes from the garden are finally red. They make a salad with them and drink tea while the sky turns orange. Sophie says: This was a good summer. We had rain, snow in the village and sun by the lake. Dad raises his cup: And many more summers to come.
